summary: TypeScript SDK retries on HTTP 400 responses, causing duplicate request + billing concern
description:
Issue summary:
Northwind AI reports that the Redwood TypeScript SDK is retrying requests that return HTTP 400 (Bad Request). They observed multiple request IDs for what they believe is a single client call, and raised concern about duplicate billing and/or duplicated side effects in their application.

Impact:
- Customer observed 2–3 identical requests sent for a single application action when the API responds with 400.
- Customer concerned this could lead to duplicate charges and/or duplicated downstream actions (they log each attempt and tie it to billing / user-visible behavior).
- Support + on-call had difficulty triaging because TS error surface did not clearly indicate whether the error was retryable and what triggered the retry.

Customer report (from email + support portal):
- SDK: @redwood-ai/sdk (TypeScript) v2.8.0 (customer-reported)
- Runtime: Node 18
- Pattern: calling chat.completions.create() with a request that sometimes returns 400 (validation failure). SDK appears to retry anyway.
- Evidence: logs show 3 request_id values within ~2 seconds, all 400, same payload.

Environment:
- Region: us-east-1
- Endpoint: api.redwoodinference.com

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Use TS SDK v2.8.0.
2) Send an invalid request that triggers a gateway/service 400 (e.g., missing required field or invalid parameter type).
3) Observe SDK retry loop (backoff) and multiple requests emitted.

Expected behavior:
- 400s should not be retried by default.
- The SDK should return a non-retryable, typed error and include request_id if present.

Actual behavior:
- In certain 400 responses, the retry middleware treats the failure as retryable and retries up to the default max attempts.
- Customer sees multiple request IDs (one per attempt).

Notes / hypotheses:
- The retry middleware appears to misclassify some 400 responses as “network errors” due to an exception during error body parsing (e.g., non-JSON error body or unexpected content-type). When parse fails, status is not propagated to the retry classifier.
- This is aligned with other parity findings: different SDKs handle “error parsing failure” differently; TS path can drop status_code and request_id.

Billing clarification (preliminary):
- Platform billing is token-based for successful generations/embeddings. 400 responses should not bill tokens; however, the customer may still see request counts and/or gateway logs that look like “multiple attempts”, and they may have internal metering tied to request volume.
- Independently of billing, duplicate attempts can create duplicate application side effects if the customer couples the API call to a non-idempotent operation.

Request IDs provided by customer (example set):
- rw_req_01HNTW9VZ9J2R3… (400)
- rw_req_01HNTW9W1P8K5A… (400)
- rw_req_01HNTW9W3F0M2C… (400)
(These were within one client action window; exact IDs stored in the private Zendesk attachment, not reproduced here.)

Ask:
- Confirm whether TS SDK is retrying 400s and under what conditions.
- Provide workaround to customer ASAP.
- Align with SDK parity initiative: retryable codes + typed error taxonomy + conformance tests to prevent regressions.
comments:
2026-01-29 09:18 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Acknowledged customer escalation. Asked for: TS SDK version, snippet showing retry config (if any), and 3 request_ids + approximate timestamps. Noted that SDK retries are expected on 429/5xx, but not on 400. Opened as P1 due to billing concern.

Shared immediate workaround: set maxRetries: 0 in client config until we confirm behavior.

2026-01-29 10:02 PT — Customer (Northwind AI) via support portal
Confirmed @redwood-ai/sdk 2.8.0, Node 18, running behind a corporate proxy. They see 3 attempts on a single call when the error is 400. They associate retries with possible double-charging because their internal cost dashboard counts requests. They asked whether Redwood bills for failed requests.

They provided logs showing three request IDs and identical payload hash.

2026-01-29 10:30 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Escalation Eng)
Pulled gateway logs for the provided request_id set. Confirmed: all three requests returned HTTP 400 with ~5–20 ms service time. No streaming involved. Response size small. Error body for at least one attempt was not JSON (content-type text/plain) due to an upstream validation error path.

Conclusion: the client truly sent 3 requests. Not a duplicate server-side processing artifact.

2026-01-29 11:15 PT — Ibrahim Khan (SDK TL) (internal note)
This matches a known parity issue: TS retry middleware can treat “failed to parse error response” as retryable because it throws before constructing the HttpError with status_code. If the retry classifier sees a generic error without status, it goes down the network-retry path. Need to ensure status is captured even if body parsing fails, and never retry 400.

Flagging Dana Lo to investigate in TS repo; also aligns with ENG-5126 error taxonomy work.

2026-01-29 13:05 PT — Dana Lo (TS SDK Owner)
Reproduced locally with v2.8.0:
- When error response is JSON, status=400 is preserved and shouldRetry=false.
- When error response is text/plain (or JSON parse throws), the SDK throws a generic error prior to wrapping it, so our retry middleware sees “unknown error” and retries.

Plan:
1) Refactor error parsing so we always preserve HTTP status + headers and build a typed error even when body parsing fails.
2) Tighten shouldRetry to require an explicit retryable classification (429/5xx/408/504 + network timeouts) rather than defaulting unknown errors to retry.
3) Add conformance coverage: 400 with non-JSON body must not retry.

ETA: patch release within a week; will link PR.

2026-01-29 14:10 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Responded to customer with billing clarification:
- Redwood does not bill tokens for requests that fail with 4xx before generation.
- They may see multiple request records because the client retried.

Provided mitigation until fix is released:
- Configure client retries off (maxRetries: 0) or restrict retryableStatusCodes to [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].
- Log request_id + retry_count for correlation.

Asked whether they rely on any side-effectful behavior tied to request submission; recommended idempotency keys where applicable (even though chat/embeddings are typically safe, their surrounding workflow might not be).

2026-01-31 16:42 PT — Dana Lo
Opened fix PR and requested review: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-1298-unify-retry-middleware-and-error-shapes.json
Key changes:
- Ensure HttpError is constructed even when response body parse fails.
- Attach status_code, request_id (if present), and retryable flag.
- Update retry classifier: do not retry when status_code is 400–499 (except 408/429), regardless of parse failures.

Also added tests for non-JSON 400 response body.

2026-02-02 09:05 PT — Allison Grant (SRE/Standards)
Reviewed retry classification against standard. Confirmed retryable defaults should include 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 + network errors/timeouts, and must not include 400. Requested one additional guard: if Retry-After is present on a 4xx that is not 429, ignore it for retries.

Suggested adding telemetry fields (retry_count, status_code, request_id) to align with the parity logging plan.

2026-02-03 11:20 PT — Dana Lo
Merged fix + follow-up for Retry-After parsing/jitter alignment: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-1307-retry-after-parsing-and-backoff-jitter.json
Cut release v2.8.2.
Release notes include: “Fix: do not retry HTTP 400 when error body parsing fails; improved typed errors with request_id + retryable flag.”

2026-02-03 12:00 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Informed customer of v2.8.2 and provided upgrade guidance + confirmation steps:
- Upgrade @redwood-ai/sdk to 2.8.2.
- Run a controlled invalid request; verify only one request_id appears and retry_count remains 0.
- Keep maxRetries: 0 in prod until upgrade completes.

Re-answered billing question: token billing not incurred for these 400s; if they need an invoice-level confirmation, we can route to finance but logs indicate no successful generations on those request_ids.

2026-02-06 15:37 PT — Customer (Northwind AI)
Upgraded to 2.8.2 in staging. Confirmed no retries on 400 anymore. Their internal request counter is now consistent. Asked for a short written statement they can share internally that 4xx validation failures do not incur token charges.

No further issues.

2026-02-10 10:12 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Provided final billing statement and closed ticket. Customer confirmed resolved in production after rollout.

Follow-ups:
- Ensure conformance suite covers “400 + non-JSON body” across SDKs.
- Ensure docs/migration notes mention the retry classifier change and how to tune maxRetries.

2026-02-10 10:20 PT — Ibrahim Khan (internal)
Logged as an input to SDK parity effort: this bug is a concrete example of why error taxonomy must preserve status_code/request_id even on parse failures. Will reference in parity matrix and conformance fixtures.
resolution: Resolved in TypeScript SDK v2.8.2 by ensuring HTTP status/request_id are preserved even when error-body parsing fails, and by tightening retry classification so 400 is never retried by default. Customer mitigated by disabling retries until upgrade. Billing concern addressed: 4xx validation failures did not incur token charges.
customer_visible_outcome: Customer upgraded to TS SDK v2.8.2; confirmed 400 responses are not retried and internal metering no longer shows duplicate attempts. Provided written clarification that 4xx validation errors do not incur token billing.
